greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen. May the grace and peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, who crowns his saints with glory, be with you all.
penitential:

Christ Jesus, you are the light that shines in the darkness, have mercy on us.
Lord Jesus, you are the hope of those who sleep in your peace, have mercy on us.

homily:
We often look at the world and see things that seem meant to last forever. We look at the stone walls of a great cathedral, or the carefully constructed systems of our own lives—the plans we make, the careers we build, the routines that give our days their shape—and we assume they are permanent. We count on the stones remaining where they were laid. But the Gospel today gives us a startling, honest, and ultimately liberating perspective. Jesus stands before the temple, a place of immense beauty and significance, and he says, 'All that you see here—the days will come when there will not be left a stone upon another stone that will not be thrown down.'

I want you to hold onto this image: the stone. Think of the way we build our lives, stone by stone. We build with our hopes, our ambitions, our daily habits, and our deep, abiding loves. Think of Benjamin Vo. Think of the way he built his life—not with the heavy, cold stones of ego, but with the vibrant, living stones of curiosity and kindness. He was a boy who loved the mechanics of flight, the logic of software, and the warmth of his family. He was a boy who, in his fifteen years, gathered experiences like precious stones: the trips across the globe, the shared moments of laughter on a bridge in autumn, the quiet joy of airport spotting with his father. He was a boy who understood that life is a structure of relationships, a temple of love that he tended with a gentle, brilliant spirit. But we also know that the stones of this world are fragile. We know that the house feels different now. The silence in the rooms where he once walked, the absence of his voice in the morning, the sudden, sharp awareness that the life we knew has shifted—this is the reality of the stones being moved. It is the ache of a heart that is trying to reconcile the beauty of what was with the silence of what is.

Let us tell the truth of the heart before we look for the comfort. Alan, Thao, Ryan, and all of you who hold the memory of Benjamin as a sacred trust: five months have passed. The calendar page turns, but the heart often stays in the room where he last smiled. We know the reality of your quiet house. We know the moments when the silence becomes a weight, when the habits of a lifetime—the quick laugh, the bright smile, the way he would share his dreams of 'con chim airlines'—are suddenly met with an empty space. You are grieving. You are carrying a cross that is heavy, real, and unrelenting. You are allowed to be tired. You are allowed to feel the sudden ache when a memory ambushes you in the middle of an ordinary day. Do not pretend the weight is lighter than it is. Do not rush to be ‘strong’ for the sake of others if your heart is currently breaking. Your honesty before God is the most authentic prayer you can offer. Your tears are not a lack of faith; they are the language of love that has no place left to go.

And let us gently lift one particular stone from your hearts today—a stone that grief often slips into our pockets without us noticing. Sometimes, when a family suffers an unimaginable loss, the mind begins to circle back, whispering quiet, unfair questions. Did we miss a sign? Could we have done something more? Could we have watched closer? Let us lay that burden down right here at the altar. You missed nothing. You loved Benjamin with a completeness that filled his fifteen years with the richness of a lifetime—traveling the globe together, sharing quiet stories, and walking side by side as a family of four. You were the exact parents and the exact brother that Benjamin needed. Let that heavy stone fall; you are absolved, and you are held. You did not fail him in any way. You were the light in his life, just as he was the light in yours. Some things in this life are simply beyond our control, and God does not hold you responsible for the mysteries of the cross. You are held in His mercy, not judged by your sorrow. You are not to blame for the randomness of the world’s living. You are simply loved.

Now, let the Gospel break into that quiet room. Jesus warns us not to be terrified by the upheaval of the world. He tells us that nation will rise against nation, that there will be signs in the sky, that the very foundations will shake. But he says something crucial: 'Do not be terrified.' This is the hinge of the mystery. When the stones of our life are shaken, when the familiar world is thrown down, we are not left in the rubble. We are invited to look up. The Book of Revelation speaks of the harvest, of the Son of Man sitting on a white cloud with a sharp sickle. It sounds like a scene of judgment, but in the light of the Gospel, it is a scene of gathering. The harvest is not the end of the grain; it is the fulfillment of its purpose. It is the moment the fruit is brought into the barn, the moment the labor of the season is realized. Benjamin is the harvest of the Lord’s love. He was a boy who lived with a heart open to the world, a boy who, when he was just fifteen, felt the weight of his uncle William’s suffering and wanted to hand over his entire piggy bank—his entire security—to help. He didn't need to break it, he didn't need to empty it; the offering itself was the harvest of his soul. It was the pure, unadulterated desire to be a blessing to someone else. That is the fruit that God gathers. That is the life that is not lost in the shaking of the world.

Consider the image of the stone again. In the New Jerusalem, the foundations are made of precious jewels. The stones that are 'thrown down' here are not destroyed; they are transformed. They are being rebuilt into a temple that cannot be shaken. Benjamin is part of that new architecture. He is standing in the presence of the Lamb, fully alive, fully restored, and fully embraced by the Father. He is the boy who loved to dream, the boy who giggled at the idea of his own airline, the boy who looked at the world with such profound curiosity. He is all of that, and he is with the God of the living. He is the firstfruits of the promise, waiting for the day when the family of four is whole again. He is watching over you with a love that has been purified and perfected. Think of the dream Alan had, where you and Ben were standing outside room 419, and he said with that earnest, familiar voice, 'Ba ơi, test nào con cũng qua hết... Không sao đâu, con sẽ dõi theo ba mẹ.' That dream was a whisper from heaven. It was the assurance that he has passed every test, that he is whole, and that he is watching over you with a smile. He is the one who has already crossed the threshold into the light, and he is cheering you on.

Ryan, you are a brother who carries a unique, holy weight. You know the memories better than anyone. You know the games you coded, the dreams you shared, the simple, everyday life of being brothers. You are not just a brother who remains; you are a brother who continues the story. When you look at the sky, when you think of the future, remember that you are not doing it alone. You are carrying the legacy of his joy. You are a witness to the world that love is not a finite resource. It is a well that never runs dry. Keep being the boy who reaches out. Keep being the one who values the small, human moments. You are a vital part of this family of four, and your life is a testament to the fact that love is the most durable thing we possess. Your brother's love is not gone; it is woven into the very fabric of who you are becoming. He is cheering for you, and he is walking with you in the quiet places of your heart. You are the one who carries his laughter forward. You are the one who keeps the melody alive.

To everyone tuning in from afar—especially other children who are carrying heavy crosses of suffering, and every family whose home feels too quiet today—hear this: you are seen by God. You are not forgotten. The Lord draws closest to the brokenhearted, and His mercy is broad enough to hold every single one of our tears. You are not a broken family. You are a family of four, and you are being held in the palm of God's hand. The Lamb who was slain is the Lamb who is risen, and he is the one who promises that one day, every tear will be wiped away, and we will see clearly that love was the only thing that ever mattered. The God of the living is the God who is with you right now in this very room, in the silence, in the ache, and in the hope that refuses to die.

So, what do you carry out the door today? Not a summary, not a heavy burden, but one small, doable thing: when the grief rises and the house feels too quiet, pause. Close your eyes. Breathe in. Imagine the Lord reaching into the silence, and imagine Benjamin standing beside you, smiling that bright, easy grin, looking out toward an endless horizon, dreaming of his next journey. Let yourself be gathered into the peace of Christ. Walk out knowing that you are loved, that you are not to blame, and that the one who went before you is waiting at the door of eternity. Keep your heart open to that truth. Keep your eyes on the light. And remember that he is watching over you, always, with love that knows no end. Amen.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, may his face shine upon you and be gracious to you, and may he give you his peace. In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
standing_petitions: For our beloved Ben and all who have gone before us, that they may rest in the eternal light of Christ and find joy in the banquet of heaven, we pray to the Lord.
For all who carry the weight of grief, that God may console their hearts, strengthen their spirits, and fill them with the hope of the Resurrection, we pray to the Lord.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
I, John, looked and there was a white cloud,
and sitting on the cloud one who looked like a son of man,
with a gold crown on his head and a sharp sickle in his hand.
Another angel came out of the temple,
crying out in a loud voice to the one sitting on the cloud,
“Use your sickle and reap the harvest,
for the time to reap has come,
because the earth’s harvest is fully ripe.”
So the one who was sitting on the cloud swung his sickle over the earth,
and the earth was harvested.Then another angel came out of the temple in heaven
who also had a sharp sickle.
Then another angel came from the altar, who was in charge of the fire,
and cried out in a loud voice
to the one who had the sharp sickle,
“Use your sharp sickle and cut the clusters from the earth’s vines,
for its grapes are ripe.”
So the angel swung his sickle over the earth and cut the earth’s vintage.
He threw it into the great wine press of God’s fury.

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R. (13b) The Lord comes to judge the earth.
Say among the nations: The LORD is king.
He has made the world firm, not to be moved;
he governs the peoples with equity.
R. The Lord comes to judge the earth.
Let the heavens be glad and the earth rejoice;
let the sea and what fills it resound;
let the plains be joyful and all that is in them!
Then shall all the trees of the forest exult.
R. The Lord comes to judge the earth.
Before the LORD, for he comes;
for he comes to rule the earth.
He shall rule the world with justice 
and the peoples with his constancy.
R. The Lord comes to judge the earth.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
While some people were speaking about
how the temple was adorned with costly stones and votive offerings,
Jesus said, “All that you see here–
the days will come when there will not be left
a stone upon another stone that will not be thrown down.”Then they asked him,
“Teacher, when will this happen?
And what sign will there be when all these things are about to happen?” 
He answered,
“See that you not be deceived,
for many will come in my name, saying,
‘I am he,’ and ‘The time has come.’ 
Do not follow them! 
When you hear of wars and insurrections,
do not be terrified; for such things must happen first,
but it will not immediately be the end.” 
Then he said to them,
“Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. 
There will be powerful earthquakes, famines, and plagues
from place to place;
and awesome sights and mighty signs will come from the sky.”

Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever
